Subject: Redwood pricing options for 3yr commit / conversion credit question

Hi Jordan,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the perf numbers look promising. Procurement is building a recommendation for the execs and they asked me to get a formal pricing structure for a 3‑year committed prepay. A few specifics we need covered:

- We expect to start at ~75k tokens/month in Q3 and reach ~1.2M tokens/month by year 3 (attached forecast).
- Two payment options under consideration: (A) single upfront prepay for years 1–3, or (B) annual prepay with true‑ups.

- Any ramp breakpoints you recommend to keep latency/cost predictable?

Can you send a proposal with suggested term discount, conversion credit mechanics, and sample payment schedule? We’ll loop in legal/procurement after the business approves.

Hi Lana —

Thanks for the clear asks and the forecast. I attached a concise term sheet with two structured options and a recommended ramp schedule. High level summary below:

Option A — 3yr Upfront Prepay (preferred economics)
- 20% blended term discount off list (applied to committed units).
- Conversion credit: unused committed units can be converted into next-year credit up to 25% of that year’s commit at 50% value (i.e., 50% of the price applied as credit toward future usage).
- Ramp: auto‑scale breakpoints at 3x/year incremental buckets to preserve latency SLOs

Option B — Annual Prepay with True‑ups
- Year 1 discount: 12% (on annual prepay).
- True‑up window: quarterly true‑ups or annual reconciliation; unused credit carries forward 1 year at 40% value.

I’ve looped in Laura to confirm there aren’t contract constraints and cc’d a finance lead (if we need a variance). If BlueRiver can do >75% upfront, we may be able to increase the blended discount by up to 3 points.

Next step: if either option looks workable, I can send a version of the term sheet and an example payment schedule for internal approvals.

Best,
Jordan Blake

Jordan —

Thanks for the heads up. A couple of legal/contract flags to consider before we promise conversion credit mechanics:

- Conversion credits need explicit lifecycle language: what happens on termination/renewal and if BlueRiver reduces commitment mid‑term. Suggest limiting conversion credits to no more than 2 roll‑forwards across the 3 years.
- For the 50% value you proposed on conversion credit, we should define whether the credit applies to list or net (after discount). Recommend applying to net for simplicity.
- Add an overage fallback: if usage spikes beyond committed buckets and we don’t have available capacity, we need an automatic fallback pricing for immediate overage in month at standard on‑demand rates (no discount).

If finance is comfortable with the blended rate and the accounting treatment for upfront revenue, we can approve the term sheet with those clauses. Vivek — can you confirm revenue recognition concerns for the 20% blended discount + 3yr upfront?

—Laura
VP, Contracts & GTM Ops
laura.bennett@redwood.com

Quick finance take:

- Revenue recognition: Upfront prepay for 3 years would be deferred and recognized over the service period; the blended discount doesn’t change deferral but does change ARR math — fine as long as we have minimum cash cover for FY26.
- Cash: If BlueRiver can do 80% upfront (or 100%), recommend we sweeten the discount to 22% (one‑time approval). If they want annual prepay, the 12% Y1 discount is fine.
- Credits: conversion credit at 50% net value is acceptable if we cap total convertibility to 25% of original commit per year and max 2 roll‑forwards as Laura suggested. That preserves revenue visibility.

I’m OK to sign off on a final term sheet with the following conditional approval: 22% blended discount if upfront >=80% for the 3yr total; otherwise 20% blended. Add the legal lifecycle language and the overage fallback.

—Vivek
